walkthroughs.body_html:
Between 1577 and 1580 Francis Drake sailed round the world in the Golden Hind.

He raided Spanish ports and treasure ships. Elizabeth knighted him on his return — angering Philip II of Spain. Drake captured £140,000 of Spanish silver — twice the Crown's annual income.

The 1585 Treaty of Nonsuch sent English troops to help Dutch Protestants against Spain.

In 1587 Drake raided Cadiz — burning 30 ships and delaying the Armada a year. Philip II planned invasion to restore Catholicism and avenge Mary's execution.

Philip's fleet of 130 ships sailed from Lisbon in May 1588.

It reached Calais but met English fireships in the night. The Battle of Gravelines (8 August 1588) scattered it. Storms — the Protestant Wind — wrecked the ships round Scotland and Ireland. Only 67 returned home.
